articles.title: British air stewardess accused of being a 'drug mule' forced to move prison after riots in Sri Lanka leave 30 dead
articles.description: A British air stewardess in a Sri Lankan jail, accused of being a "drug mule", was forced to move after prison riots left 30 dead. Charlotte May Lee, 22, was arrested in South Asia last year after officials were alleged to have found 46kg of cannabis, worth £1.2million, in her luggage when she arrived on a flight from Thailand. If charged and convicted, the part-time beautician is looking at a maximum 25-year sentence behind bars in Sri Lanka's maximum security prison, Welikada in Colombo. Yet to receive a formal charge, the 22-year-old has now spent 18 months banged up in the notorious, overcrowded Negombo jail, where two days of violence left more than 100 injured back in July. The chaos unravelled as two groups of inmates were alleged to have nabbed guards' guns and turned fire on each other as shots were heard. The riots were said to have traumatised the British inmate, who has now been moved to a jail in north west Sri Lanka, Kuliyappitiya. The insider said: "Charlotte was traumatised by the riots, a lot of people lost their lives. "When the riots happened at Negombo, people were worried for her safety but she survived and has been moved. "She is alone in a foreign country, it’s very frightening. But she is now in Kuliyappitiya prison." Sources said that Ms Lee is now "coping well" after moving institutions, The Mirror said. In the meantime, Ms Lee is now attempting to learn the native tongue to help with communicating with other Sri Lankan inmates. They told the paper the stewardess was "desperate to get home but knows there’s nothing she can do" while fighting her case. LATEST DEVELOPMENTS: Donald Trump calls Norway a 's**t house country' and says he 'doesn't want anybody from there' in US Senior Isis-linked terrorist who plotted to kidnap British ambassador 'smuggled himself into UK' Serbia's streets ERUPT after conservative leader concedes election defeat to student-led movement Upon her arrest, local police showed the images of the vacuum-packed drugs which authorities alleged were stuffed into Ms Lee's suitcases. However, the 22-year-old said the drugs were put into her baggage while in Bangkok without her knowledge. A friend of Ms Lee previously told The Sun: "She’s been told if convicted, because of the size of the drugs haul, she’s looking at between 20 and 25 years in jail. "British Embassy staff warned her she’s going nowhere soon." The Negombo jail is infamous for its horrendous conditions - with Ms Lee explaining that she sleeps on the concrete floor of a cell holding five women, forced to use her clothes as a pillow. Speaking in court, she said: "I have never been to prison and I've never been to Sri Lanka. "This heat and just sitting on a concrete floor all of the time." She added: "There are people from so many different countries who have been here for two years, two-and-a-half years. And it's still just waiting and no-one actually knows anything." articles.title: Jordan says its air force struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after church attack
articles.description: Jordan said on Monday its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the suspects behind last weeks deadly church attack in the kingdom were linked to terrorist groups operating there The armed forces said the operation was conducted in coordination with Damascus There was no immediate comment from Syrian authorities Five civilians including women and children were killed as a result of the Jordanian strikes a health official told Syrias state news agency
